title: [Optional] Live Deployment to Test Internet Identity Authentication
summary: Wires the Internet Identity login into the token app: Faucet and Transfer build an authenticated actor so msg.caller becomes the logged-in user's principal. Because the local dfx replica cannot complete the Internet Identity sign-off, the project is deployed to the live Internet Computer to test it, and the user's principal is surfaced in the UI via props.

concepts.heading: Goal: make msg.caller the authenticated principal
points: Until now Faucet.jsx called payOut() on the imported default actor (token), which talks to the canister anonymously, so the caller was always the anonymous principal.
To pay out to the real logged-in user, the component needs its own actor that carries the user's identity, then calls payOut() on that actor instead.
Inside the Motoko payOut, msg.caller then resolves to the authenticated user's principal, and that account receives the tokens.

concepts.heading: Imports needed in the component
points: AuthClient comes from the @dfinity/auth-client package (already used in index.jsx for login).
From the generated declarations folder, import canisterId and createActor in addition to the default token actor. These already exist in the declarations index.js generated for the project.

createActor builds a canister handle (an 'actor') for a given canister id; it accepts an options object. canisterId is filled in from an environment variable at build time, holding the backend canister's principal.

concepts.heading: Building the authenticated actor inside the click handler
points: After the button is disabled, call await AuthClient.create() to get a client. It restores the session saved by the earlier login.
Call await authClient.getIdentity() to get the identity object of the logged-in user. Both awaits are required; forgetting one yields a promise instead of the value.
Call createActor(canisterId, { agentOptions: { identity } }). The second argument is the options object; agentOptions is passed to the underlying HTTP agent, which signs requests with that identity.
Store the result in a const such as authenticatedCanister and call authenticatedCanister.payOut() in place of token.payOut().
Typo-prone spots: createActor, getIdentity, matching braces and commas around the nested objects.

concepts.heading: Why it cannot be tested locally
points: Clicking the faucet button against the local dfx replica returns a 403 error. The local replica is a simulation for development; the Internet Identity sign-off flow only works against the live network.
So the project must be deployed to the mainnet ('ic' network). Enough cycles are needed; if low, convert ICP to cycles as shown in earlier lessons.
Follow the README step by step by copying commands rather than retyping them, since they are error-prone.

concepts.heading: Live deployment steps
points: Deploy all canisters: dfx deploy --network ic. Takes a couple of minutes if cycles suffice.
Find the live backend canister id (differs from the local one): dfx canister --network ic id token.
Wrap it in a Candid principal literal and store in a shell variable (LIVE_CANISTER_KEY), then echo it to check that the format is principal "...".

Transfer half the supply to the canister so the faucet has tokens to give out: dfx canister --network ic call token transfer with the variable and the amount. A success result confirms it. The owner keeps the other half.
Find the frontend (assets) canister id: dfx canister --network ic id token_assets. Open it in a browser as <id>.raw.ic0.app, which serves the deployed React app.
Allow pop-ups first: the Internet Identity login opens in a pop-up window. On the first visit the user must authenticate again, because the live site is a different origin from the local one.
Click the faucet button: success may take longer than locally because the live network latency varies. A success message proves the authenticated path works, in contrast to the earlier error.

concepts.heading: Inspecting the identity and getting the principal
points: Debug.print output from Motoko does not appear in a terminal on the live network, so logging is done on the frontend instead.
console.log(await authClient.getIdentity()) in the login handler shows an identity object with four main fields; the one of interest is _principal.

Take const identity = await authClient.getIdentity(); then const userPrincipal = identity._principal.toString(). The raw property is an object; toString() converts it to the familiar readable text id.
Checking that principal's balance in the Balance component shows the 10,000 tokens claimed from the faucet, confirming the call was made as the authenticated user.
After each frontend change, redeploy with dfx deploy --network ic and refresh.

concepts.heading: Showing the principal in the UI with props
points: Pass the string down as a prop: in index.jsx render <App loggedInPrincipal={userPrincipal} />. The pattern is propName={value}.
In App, read props.loggedInPrincipal and hand it to the faucet as <Faucet userPrincipal={props.loggedInPrincipal} />.
Faucet takes props as its function parameter (a common typo is writing 'pops') and renders {props.userPrincipal} in the label text instead of the generic 'your account' wording.
Result: the faucet label displays the logged-in user's principal id without opening the console.

code_examples.caption: Faucet.jsx: claim through an authenticated actor
index.jsx: derive the principal string and pass it down
Live network commands (from the project README)
code_examples.code:
dfx deploy --network ic
dfx canister --network ic id token
LIVE_CANISTER_KEY="principal \"$( dfx canister --network ic id token )\""
echo $LIVE_CANISTER_KEY
dfx canister --network ic call token transfer "($LIVE_CANISTER_KEY, 500_000_000)"
dfx canister --network ic id token_assets
# open https://<assets-id>.raw.ic0.app

task.name: Hook the Transfer component up to the authenticated canister
task.starting_point: Faucet already uses the authenticated actor and shows the principal. Transfer.jsx still calls token.transfer on the anonymous default actor, so transferring from the logged-in account fails with insufficient funds.
task.goal: Transfer tokens from the logged-in user's account to another principal (for example an earlier anonymous account) using the same authentication pattern as the Faucet.
steps: In Transfer.jsx, import AuthClient from @dfinity/auth-client and canisterId plus createActor from the declarations; the old token import can be dropped.
In the click handler, just before the transfer call, create the client with await AuthClient.create().
Get the identity with await authClient.getIdentity().
Build const authenticatedCanister = createActor(canisterId, { agentOptions: { identity } }).
Replace token.transfer(...) with authenticatedCanister.transfer(recipient, amountToTransfer), keeping the recipient principal and amount from the form.
Deploy to the live network, refresh, enter a recipient principal and an amount, press Transfer.
task.expected_result: After a noticeable wait the feedback says Success instead of Insufficient funds; the sender's balance drops by the amount sent (200 in the demo) and the recipient's balance rises accordingly.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 41 - Create Your Own Crypto Token/41.11 Live Deployment to Test Internet Identity Authentication/DANG/src/DANG_frontend/src/components/Transfer.jsx

pitfalls: Testing locally: the Internet Identity sign-off gives a 403 on the local replica; deploy to the ic network.
Missing an await on AuthClient.create() or getIdentity().
Forgetting to redeploy after each frontend change, or running low on cycles.
Popups blocked, so the login window never appears.
Writing props as 'pops' or mismatching the prop name between index.jsx, App and Faucet.

(Extra) The reference repo is a newer dfx scaffold: canisters are DANG_backend and DANG_frontend (not token and token_assets), it has a typo prop loogedInPrincipal used consistently, and Faucet is the only component that displays the principal.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (section 41 has no playground file).
gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Acting as a logged-in user': blurb explaining anonymous vs authenticated callers and why a backend needs msg.caller.

Tasks: 1) create an AuthClient and read its identity; 2) build an actor with createActor and agentOptions; 3) pass a principal down as props and render it; 4) convert a second component to the authenticated actor; 5) predict what msg.caller would be before and after.
Starter code: a small React component with a stub 'api' object whose methods return the caller id.
Explore demo idea: a mock identity switcher (anonymous vs logged in) that shows which principal the fake canister sees and how balances change after a payOut and transfer.
